verses.original: Φῆστος οὖν ἐπιβὰς τῇ ἐπαρχείᾳ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀνέβη εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀπὸ Καισαρείας
verses.transliteration: Phēstos oun epibas tē eparcheia meta treis hēmeras anebē eis Hierosolyma apo Kaisareias
verses.literal: Three days after his arrival in the province Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem

verses.original: ἐνεφάνισάν τε αὐτῷ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρῶτοι τῶν Ἰουδαίων κατὰ τοῦ Παύλου καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν
verses.transliteration: enephanisan te autō hoi archiereis kai hoi prōtoi tōn Ioudaiōn kata tou Paulou kai parekaloun auton
verses.literal: where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case . . . against Paul They urged Festus

verses.original: αἰτούμενοι χάριν κατ’ αὐτοῦ ὅπως μεταπέμψηται αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ ἐνέδραν ποιοῦντες ἀνελεῖν αὐτὸν κατὰ τὴν ὁδόν
verses.transliteration: aitoumenoi charin kat’ autou hopōs metapempsētai auton eis Ierousalēm enedran poiountes anelein auton kata tēn hodon
verses.literal: to grant them a concession against Paul by summoning him to Jerusalem because they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way

verses.original: Ὁ μὲν οὖν Φῆστος ἀπεκρίθη τηρεῖσθαι τὸν Παῦλον εἰς Καισάρειαν ἑαυτὸν δὲ μέλλειν ἐν τάχει ἐκπορεύεσθαι
verses.transliteration: Ho men oun Phēstos apekrithē tēreisthai ton Paulon eis Kaisareian heauton de mellein en tachei ekporeuesthai
verses.literal: But - Festus replied Paul is being held in Caesarea and I myself am going there soon

verses.original: Οἱ οὖν ἐν ὑμῖν φησίν Δυνατοὶ συνκαταβάντες εἴ τί ἐστιν ἐν τῷ ἀνδρὶ ἄτοπον κατηγορείτωσαν αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Hoi oun en hymin phēsin Dynatoi synkatabantes ei ti estin en tō andri atopon katēgoreitōsan autou
verses.literal: So if this man has done anything wrong let some of your leaders come down with me and accuse him there

verses.original: Διατρίψας δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς ἡμέρας οὐ πλείους ὀκτὼ ἢ δέκα καταβὰς εἰς Καισάρειαν τῇ ἐπαύριον καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσεν τὸν Παῦλον ἀχθῆναι
verses.transliteration: Diatripsas de en autois hēmeras ou pleious oktō ē deka katabas eis Kaisareian tē epaurion kathisas epi tou bēmatos ekeleusen ton Paulon achthēnai
verses.literal: After spending no more than eight or ten days with them Festus went down to Caesarea The next day he sat on the judgment seat and ordered that Paul be brought in

verses.original: παραγενομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ περιέστησαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων καταβεβηκότες Ἰουδαῖοι πολλὰ καὶ βαρέα αἰτιώματα καταφέροντες ἃ οὐκ ἴσχυον ἀποδεῖξαι
verses.transliteration: paragenomenou de autou periestēsan auton hoi apo Hierosolymōn katabebēkotes Ioudaioi polla kai barea aitiōmata katapherontes ha ouk ischyon apodeixai
verses.literal: When Paul arrived the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him bringing many serious charges that they could not prove

verses.original: Τοῦ Παύλου ἀπολογουμένου ὅτι Οὔτε εἰς τὸν νόμον τῶν Ἰουδαίων οὔτε εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν οὔτε εἰς Καίσαρά τι ἥμαρτον
verses.transliteration: Tou Paulou apologoumenou hoti Oute eis ton nomon tōn Ioudaiōn oute eis to hieron oute eis Kaisara ti hēmarton
verses.literal: Then Paul made his defense I have committed no offense . . . . . . against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar

verses.original: Ὁ Φῆστος δὲ θέλων τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις χάριν καταθέσθαι ἀποκριθεὶς τῷ Παύλῳ εἶπεν Θέλεις εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἀναβὰς ἐκεῖ περὶ τούτων κριθῆναι ἐπ’ ἐμοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ho Phēstos de thelōn tois Ioudaiois charin katathesthai apokritheis tō Paulō eipen Theleis eis Hierosolyma anabas ekei peri toutōn krithēnai ep’ emou
verses.literal: But Festus wishing to do the Jews a favor . . . . . . . . . said to Paul Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges

verses.original: Εἶπεν δὲ ὁ Παῦλος Ἑστὼς ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος Καίσαρος εἰμι οὗ με δεῖ κρίνεσθαι Ἰουδαίους οὐδὲν ἠδίκησα ὡς καὶ σὺ κάλλιον ἐπιγινώσκεις
verses.transliteration: Eipen de ho Paulos Hestōs epi tou bēmatos Kaisaros eimi hou me dei krinesthai Ioudaious ouden ēdikēsa hōs kai sy kallion epiginōskeis
verses.literal: Paul replied I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar where I ought to be tried I have done nothing wrong . . . to the Jews as you yourself know very well

verses.original: εἰ μὲν οὖν ἀδικῶ καὶ ἄξιον θανάτου πέπραχά τι οὐ παραιτοῦμαι τὸ ἀποθανεῖν εἰ δὲ οὐδέν ἐστιν ὧν οὗτοι κατηγοροῦσίν μου οὐδείς με δύναται αὐτοῖς χαρίσασθαι Καίσαρα ἐπικαλοῦμαι
verses.transliteration: ei men oun adikō kai axion thanatou pepracha ti ou paraitoumai to apothanein ei de ouden estin hōn houtoi katēgorousin mou oudeis me dynatai autois charisasthai Kaisara epikaloumai
verses.literal: If however . . . I am guilty of anything worthy of death I do not refuse to die But if there is no truth to their accusations against me no one has the right to hand me over . . . to them I appeal to Caesar

verses.original: Τότε ὁ Φῆστος συλλαλήσας μετὰ τοῦ συμβουλίου ἀπεκρίθη Καίσαρα ἐπικέκλησαι ἐπὶ Καίσαρα πορεύσῃ
verses.transliteration: Tote ho Phēstos syllalēsas meta tou symbouliou apekrithē Kaisara epikeklēsai epi Kaisara poreusē
verses.literal: Then Festus conferred with his council and replied You have appealed to Caesar To Caesar you will go

verses.original: Ἡμερῶν δὲ διαγενομένων τινῶν Ἀγρίππας ὁ βασιλεὺς καὶ Βερνίκη κατήντησαν εἰς Καισάρειαν ἀσπασάμενοι τὸν Φῆστον
verses.transliteration: Hēmerōn de diagenomenōn tinōn Agrippas ho basileus kai Bernikē katēntēsan eis Kaisareian aspasamenoi ton Phēston
verses.literal: After several days had passed King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus

verses.original: ὡς δὲ πλείους ἡμέρας διέτριβον ἐκεῖ ὁ Φῆστος τῷ βασιλεῖ ἀνέθετο τὰ κατὰ τὸν Παῦλον λέγων Ἀνήρ τίς ἐστιν καταλελειμμένος ὑπὸ Φήλικος δέσμιος
verses.transliteration: hōs de pleious hēmeras dietribon ekei ho Phēstos tō basilei anetheto ta kata ton Paulon legōn Anēr tis estin kataleleimmenos hypo Phēlikos desmios
verses.literal: Since . . . they were staying . . . several days Festus laid out Paul’s case before the king There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison

verses.original: περὶ οὗ γενομένου μου εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐνεφάνισαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τῶν Ἰουδαίων αἰτούμενοι κατ’ αὐτοῦ καταδίκην
verses.transliteration: peri hou genomenou mou eis Hierosolyma enephanisan hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi tōn Ioudaiōn aitoumenoi kat’ autou katadikēn
verses.literal: While I was in Jerusalem the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case . . . . . . and requested a judgment against him

verses.original: πρὸς οὓς ἀπεκρίθην ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν ἔθος Ῥωμαίοις χαρίζεσθαί τινα ἄνθρωπον πρὶν ἢ ὁ κατηγορούμενος κατὰ πρόσωπον ἔχοι τοὺς κατηγόρους τόπον τε ἀπολογίας λάβοι περὶ τοῦ ἐγκλήματος
verses.transliteration: pros hous apekrithēn hoti ouk estin ethos Rhōmaiois charizesthai tina anthrōpon prin ē ho katēgoroumenos kata prosōpon echoi tous katēgorous topon te apologias laboi peri tou enklēmatos
verses.literal: I told them that it is not the Roman custom . . . to hand a man over before he . . . has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges

verses.original: Συνελθόντων οὖν αὐτῶν ἐνθάδε ἀναβολὴν μηδεμίαν ποιησάμενος τῇ ἑξῆς καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκέλευσα ἀχθῆναι τὸν ἄνδρα
verses.transliteration: Synelthontōn oun autōn enthade anabolēn mēdemian poiēsamenos tē hexēs kathisas epi tou bēmatos ekeleusa achthēnai ton andra
verses.literal: So when they came here with me I did not delay The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in

verses.original: περὶ οὗ σταθέντες οἱ κατήγοροι οὐδεμίαν αἰτίαν ἔφερον ὧν ἐγὼ ὑπενόουν πονηρῶν
verses.transliteration: peri hou stathentes hoi katēgoroi oudemian aitian epheron hōn egō hypenooun ponērōn
verses.literal: But when his accusers rose to speak they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected

verses.original: ζητήματα δέ τινα περὶ τῆς ἰδίας δεισιδαιμονίας εἶχον πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ περί τινος Ἰησοῦ τεθνηκότος ὃν ἔφασκεν ὁ Παῦλος ζῆν
verses.transliteration: zētēmata de tina peri tēs idias deisidaimonias eichon pros auton kai peri tinos Iēsou tethnēkotos hon ephasken ho Paulos zēn
verses.literal: They only had some contentions with him regarding their own religion and a certain Jesus who had died but whom Paul affirmed to be alive

verses.original: Ἀπορούμενος δὲ ἐγὼ τὴν περὶ τούτων ζήτησιν ἔλεγον εἰ βούλοιτο πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα κἀκεῖ κρίνεσθαι περὶ τούτων
verses.transliteration: Aporoumenos de egō tēn peri toutōn zētēsin elegon ei bouloito poreuesthai eis Hierosolyma kakei krinesthai peri toutōn
verses.literal: Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters I asked if he was willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried there on these charges

verses.original: τοῦ δὲ Παύλου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τηρηθῆναι αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ διάγνωσιν ἐκέλευσα τηρεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ἕως οὗ ἀναπέμψω αὐτὸν πρὸς Καίσαρα
verses.transliteration: tou de Paulou epikalesamenou tērēthēnai auton eis tēn tou Sebastou diagnōsin ekeleusa tēreisthai auton heōs hou anapempsō auton pros Kaisara
verses.literal: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor I ordered that he be held until I could send him to Caesar

verses.original: Ἀγρίππας δὲ πρὸς τὸν Φῆστον Ἐβουλόμην καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀκοῦσαι Αὔριον φησίν Ἀκούσῃ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Agrippas de pros ton Phēston Eboulomēn kai autos tou anthrōpou akousai Aurion phēsin Akousē autou
verses.literal: Then Agrippa said to Festus I would like to hear this man myself Tomorrow you will hear him Festus declared

verses.original: Τῇ οὖν ἐπαύριον ἐλθόντος τοῦ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῆς Βερνίκης μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας καὶ εἰσελθόντων εἰς τὸ ἀκροατήριον σύν τε χιλιάρχοις καὶ ἀνδράσιν τοῖς κατ’ ἐξοχὴν τῆς πόλεως καὶ κελεύσαντος τοῦ Φήστου ἤχθη ὁ Παῦλος
verses.transliteration: Tē oun epaurion elthontos tou Agrippa kai tēs Bernikēs meta pollēs phantasias kai eiselthontōn eis to akroatērion syn te chiliarchois kai andrasin tois kat’ exochēn tēs poleōs kai keleusantos tou Phēstou ēchthē ho Paulos
verses.literal: The next day Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered . . . the auditorium along with the commanders and leading men of the city And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in

verses.original: Καί φησιν ὁ Φῆστος Ἀγρίππα βασιλεῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ συμπαρόντες ἡμῖν ἄνδρες θεωρεῖτε τοῦτον περὶ οὗ ἅπαν τὸ πλῆθος τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἐνέτυχόν μοι ἔν τε Ἱεροσολύμοις καὶ ἐνθάδε βοῶντες μὴ δεῖν αὐτὸν ζῆν μηκέτι
verses.transliteration: Kai phēsin ho Phēstos Agrippa basileu kai pantes hoi symparontes hēmin andres theōreite touton peri hou hapan to plēthos tōn Ioudaiōn enetychon moi en te Hierosolymois kai enthade boōntes mē dein auton zēn mēketi
verses.literal: Then Festus said King Agrippa and all who are present with us you see this man The whole Jewish community has petitioned me about him both here and in Jerusalem crying out that he ought not to live any longer

verses.original: ἐγὼ δὲ κατελαβόμην μηδὲν ἄξιον αὐτὸν θανάτου πεπραχέναι αὐτοῦ δὲ τούτου ἐπικαλεσαμένου τὸν Σεβαστὸν ἔκρινα πέμπειν
verses.transliteration: egō de katelabomēn mēden axion auton thanatou peprachenai autou de toutou epikalesamenou ton Sebaston ekrina pempein
verses.literal: But I found he had done nothing worthy of death and since he . . . has now appealed to the Emperor I decided to send him

verses.original: περὶ οὗ ἀσφαλές τι γράψαι τῷ κυρίῳ οὐκ ἔχω διὸ προήγαγον αὐτὸν ἐφ’ ὑμῶν καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ σοῦ βασιλεῦ Ἀγρίππα ὅπως τῆς ἀνακρίσεως γενομένης σχῶ τί γράψω
verses.transliteration: peri hou asphales ti grapsai tō kyriō ouk echō dio proēgagon auton eph’ hymōn kai malista epi sou basileu Agrippa hopōs tēs anakriseōs genomenēs schō ti grapsō
verses.literal: I have nothing . . . definite to write to our sovereign about him Therefore I have brought him before all of you and especially before you King Agrippa so that after this inquiry . . . I may have something to write

verses.original: ἄλογον γάρ μοι δοκεῖ πέμποντα δέσμιον μὴ καὶ τὰς κατ’ αὐτοῦ αἰτίας σημᾶναι
verses.transliteration: alogon gar moi dokei pemponta desmion mē kai tas kat’ autou aitias sēmanai
verses.literal: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without . . . specifying the charges against him
